oracle.project: exact Gaussian-process log marginal likelihood by an explicit Cholesky factorisation over the declared grid
oracle.algorithm: squared-exponential kernel, exact Cholesky NLML = 1/2 y'K^-1 y + sum log L_ii + n/2 log 2 pi over the data-scaled hyperparameter grid, on the mean-centred outcome; argmin cell and runner-up value
context_only_outputs: reference.runner_up_nlml (regenerated, not compared by the executing assertion)

reference_review.scope: The 5 x 5 data-scaled hyperparameter grid for 24 points of sin(1.3x) + 0.18 cos(3.1x): the selected length scale, noise standard deviation, signal variance and prior mean, and the exact NLML of the selected and runner-up cells.
reference_review.independence_basis: The generator evaluates the exact negative log marginal likelihood of every grid cell with a Cholesky factorisation written in the script, picks the minimum and reproduces the frozen selected cell, variance, mean, NLML (-27.089213) and runner-up NLML to 1e-9 relative. It imports no Antecedent code and no numerical package. The squared-exponential kernel form is the one under which the frozen NLML values are reproduced; the grid multipliers and the variance and prior-mean conventions are declared in the fixture and shared.
reference_review.historical_exposure: Original harness deleted (preserved in historical_oracle). The retained generator was written during this review from the fixture's declared inputs and the textbook definition; the product's assertion source and its data builder were read; the product fit routine was not consulted. It reproduces every frozen value, so the frozen values were not products of a faulty product run. Who first derived the earlier values is unrecorded.
reference_review.redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 generator and deterministic inputs. Python standard library only, in an isolated locked script environment, outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source is stored.
reference_review.limitations: Feature-gated consumer: the executing assertion (crates/antecedent-model/src/registry/mod.rs, gaussian_process_matches_exact_logdet_oracle) compiles only with the gaussian-process feature. It compares the four hyperparameters at relative 1e-9; the NLML values are not compared. One data set and one kernel; the selection is a grid argmin, not a continuous optimum. No predictive-accuracy or calibration claim.

historical_oracle.command: python3 <scratch script: numpy/scipy exact NLML over the grid below>
